title: Regulatory framework and unitholder rights
objectives: Describe the role of SEBI, AMFI and the key regulations.
List unitholder rights and exit options.
body_md:
**SEBI** regulates mutual funds under the **SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996**, plus circulars. **AMFI** is the industry body that runs the distributor registration and code of conduct.

## What the regulations cover

- Registration and eligibility of sponsors, trustees and AMCs.
- Scheme launch rules, offer documents and advertising.
- Investment restrictions, valuation, expenses and disclosures.
- Audit, inspection and enforcement.

## Unitholder rights

| Right | Detail |
|---|---|
| Receive statements and information | Account statements, annual report summaries |
| Redemption proceeds on time | Within the prescribed working days |
| Vote on key changes | A change in **fundamental attributes** needs unitholder approval or an **exit option** at NAV without exit load (for at least 30 days) |
| Inspect documents | Trust deed, offer documents, reports |
| Wind-up | A scheme can be wound up on a resolution of unitholders (three-fourths majority) |

## Investment limits (examples)

A scheme cannot invest in unlisted securities beyond set limits and cannot lend or borrow except for limited short-term needs.

> **Exam tip:** Know the exit option: unitholders who dislike a change in fundamental attributes can leave without load.
example: A scheme plans to change from a large-cap to a mid-cap mandate. Unitholders must be informed and given at least 30 days to exit at NAV with no exit load.
say: Unitholders have a right to exit without load if the fund changes its fundamental attributes.
SEBI sets the rules; AMFI runs distributor registration.
never: The AMC can change the scheme any time without telling anyone.
AMFI is the regulator of mutual funds.

check.q: The regulator of mutual funds in India is:
A change in fundamental attributes gives unitholders:
o: An exit option without exit load
check.why: Unitholders get an exit option at NAV with no load.

check.q: A scheme can be wound up on the resolution of:
o: Three-fourths of unitholders (or trustees under rules)
check.why: Unitholders may wind up a scheme by a three-fourths majority resolution.
